scope: Fourth-pass ASIC/pin/boot uncertainties. No CAD edits, unchanged native-test reruns, hardware operation or Vivado execution.

entries.title: ASIC electrical limits for all 117 lines
entries.known_fact: The accepted inventory is 117 logical lines. The tutorial gives a nominal 1.5 V ASIC supply, and a historical netlist wires AC_IN/IMP_TST directly to an ECP5 bank powered at 1.5 V. Custom ASIC symbol pins are passive; ERC cannot check thresholds or direction.
entries.unknown_or_missing: ASIC VIH/VIL, VOH/VOL at stated load, absolute limits, leakage/clamp current, powered-off tolerance and capacitive loading. AC_IN/IMP_TST also lack an established function, direction and permitted waveform. Supply voltage alone does not establish compatibility.
entries.failure_consequence: Wrong thresholds can corrupt data; an incorrectly driven pin or active signal into an unpowered chip can cause excess current or damage.
entries.closure_criterion: Identify the ASIC revision and obtain a designer-approved pin electrical table or pad schematic. Calculate both directions against DS181 and actual rail/ground tolerances; resolve AC_IN/IMP_TST direction and waveform before assigning I/O standards.
entries.suggested_owner: ASIC designer with FPGA hardware engineer

user_input_needed.request: Provide the actual ASIC pad/interface specification or identify the ASIC designer who can approve one. A generic 512-channel paper cannot close this.

entries.owner_status: Suggested role only; not an assigned commitment

entries.title: Map logical slots to the physical eight ASICs and shared loads
entries.known_fact: 88 returned wires expand into eight groups of eight DATA plus CLK/READ/SYNC. Other names include four recording clocks, four SPI clocks, four chip-specific L/R programming pairs and two board-shared L/R pairs.
entries.unknown_or_missing: No authoritative matrix identifies each physical ASIC/carrier/channel order, which chips each clock drives, the four stimulation-chip slots, or every receiver on a shared control. Four clocks and eight ASICs do not prove physical pairing.
entries.failure_consequence: Correct contact counts can still control the wrong chip, merge independent signals, overload a shared control or mislabel channels.
entries.closure_criterion: A reviewed routing-board schematic/table maps every logical name to physical ASIC/pad/carrier, enumerates shared loads and matches both mezzanine sides contact by contact.
entries.suggested_owner: ASIC/routing-board designer with FPGA hardware engineer

user_input_needed.request: Provide or confirm the eight-ASIC placement/group map and which chips/boards use stimulation. A marked-up routing schematic is sufficient.

entries.owner_status: Suggested role only; not an assigned commitment

entries.title: Define inactive states and power/reset transitions
entries.known_fact: PUDC_B is pulled high and the constraint fragment requests UNUSEDPIN Pullnone. Application nets have no completed external inactive-state network. The tutorial describes sequences but not a complete startup electrical contract.
entries.unknown_or_missing: Reset polarity/pulse timing, inactive levels, latch behavior, stimulation inhibit and clock start/stop rules during ramp, failed configuration, reprogramming, power loss and partial-board power.
entries.failure_consequence: ASICs can start in an unknown state or see unintended reset/programming/stimulation edges before valid firmware owns the pins.
entries.closure_criterion: An ASIC-approved power/configuration state and timing table; necessary external pulls/interlocks calculated from leakage/load bounds; verify transitions with missing clocks and either board independently powered.
entries.suggested_owner: ASIC designer and FPGA hardware/firmware engineers

user_input_needed.request: Confirm reset/stimulation inactive states through the same ASIC interface specification requested in ASIC-01; this is not a separate user engineering task.

entries.owner_status: Suggested role only; not an assigned commitment

entries.title: Assign and constrain the application pins and eight returned clocks
entries.known_fact: Prior package evidence found 150 positions on 1.5 V banks and 12 P-side clock groups for eight returned clocks. All 117 FPGA balls remain TBD. The full-system XDC constrains only local P17 at 32 MHz.
entries.unknown_or_missing: No complete ball allocation, clock-region/tree plan, source-synchronous input delays, routing skew budget, output drive/slew/fanout analysis or CDC/reset-crossing implementation.
entries.failure_consequence: A sufficient raw pin count can still fail placement, setup/hold timing or reliable sampling.
entries.closure_criterion: Using actual ASIC timing, implement one complete schematic/ball/XDC contract on the selected Vivado part. Review DRC, timing, clock-use and CDC reports with no unjustified dedicated-route overrides or unconstrained external paths.

user_input_needed.request: Engineering work; the ASIC electrical/timing source above is the external dependency.

entries.title: Select the exact FPGA ordering grade
entries.known_fact: U1 speed/temperature grade remains TBD. Present core power assumes a standard 1.0 V grade. DS181 specifies 0.92-0.98 V for -1LI.
entries.unknown_or_missing: No exact orderable speed/temperature code, operating-temperature envelope or matching implemented Vivado target is frozen.
entries.failure_consequence: Procurement could substitute an incompatible voltage variant, or the application could exceed the selected grade's timing/temperature limits.
entries.closure_criterion: Freeze a traceable standard-voltage part, confirm package/temperature/availability, use its exact tool part and close timing/power/thermal checks for that grade.

entries.title: Prove flash cold boot and recovery on the selected revision
entries.known_fact: Minimal core uses 3.3 V configuration; rail revision uses 1.8 V equivalents and CFGBVS=GND. Saved boot nets passed the prior file audit. Current AMD Artix-7 programming documentation includes MX25U12835F under the mx25u12872f alias.
entries.unknown_or_missing: Installed Vivado cfgmem selection/read-ID, programming through custom JTAG, flash startup versus rail ramp, brownout/QPI recovery and repeated cold boot are unverified.
entries.failure_consequence: A consistent schematic may still fail to load its image or lack recovery through the intended external port after interruption.
entries.closure_criterion: Board-hash-specific build/bridge; verify exact flash ID/algorithm; measure rails, INIT_B, DONE and CCLK against flash startup/reset limits; record cold/warm/brownout/reprogramming recovery and the fallback path.

entries.known_fact: The root blink build now warns it belongs to a legacy board with the removed LED and 3.3 V constraints. minimal_core has no matching bring-up target; full_system contains only core.xdc.

entries.title: Prove sample identity, frame alignment and control behavior
entries.known_fact: The tutorial describes 1024 clocks/frame, one SYNC and 16 READ events; each data wire multiplexes four ADC groups. Link arithmetic depends on extracting/packing 12-bit samples rather than forwarding 16 bits/sample.
entries.unknown_or_missing: No eight-ASIC implementation proves sample bit/order mapping, frame alignment across returned clocks, missing/extra edge detection, restart, gain/stimulation command semantics or channel identity at the PC.
entries.failure_consequence: A link can move the expected byte rate while silently mislabeling channels, losing samples or applying commands incorrectly.
entries.closure_criterion: ASIC-referenced golden vectors/channel map and timing contract; simulate edge cases, implement loss flags/counters/recovery, then compare controlled ASIC inputs/readback with recorded PC output for every channel and intended control.
